# Documentation Consistency Checklist

Use this checklist when reviewing README, architecture docs, API references, process docs, or onboarding guides.

## A. Terminology Consistency
- One concept uses one canonical term only.
- Acronyms are expanded on first use.
- Role names and component names match across all docs.
- Avoid mixed naming styles for the same object.

## B. Step Order Correctness
- Prerequisites appear before setup steps.
- Setup appears before execution and verification.
- Troubleshooting appears after normal workflow.
- No forward references to undefined steps.

## C. Prerequisite Completeness
- Runtime/version requirements are explicit.
- Required env vars and secrets are listed with source.
- Required access permissions are stated.
- Dependencies and installation commands are complete.

## D. Contradiction Detection
- Same feature is not described with conflicting behavior.
- Inputs/outputs are consistent between sections.
- API examples match documented parameter names.
- Error handling statements are consistent.

## E. Clarity and Actionability
- Every section has a clear objective.
- Long paragraphs are broken into actionable steps.
- Ambiguous words are replaced with measurable statements.
- Reader can complete tasks without guessing missing context.

## F. Output Requirements (for reviewer)
- Findings sorted by severity: Critical, Major, Minor.
- Exact replacement text provided for each Major/Critical finding.
- Open questions listed when source of truth is missing.
- Final pass/fail summary for release readiness.

## G. Template-Implementation Sync
- Every `.agent.md` / `SKILL.md` template shown inside a guide doc (e.g. `docs/agent-knowledge-guide.md` section 9) is manually diffed against the actual file it claims to represent (`.github/agents/*.agent.md`, `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md`).
- Mismatches (missing sections, outdated procedure steps, stale output contracts) are reported as Major findings, not Minor — a stale template silently regresses anyone who copies it.
- This is a manual check performed at review time; no automated sync script is required or assumed.
